Synopsis:
The player hears an uproar in the camp and  think the owlbear’s turned on Scratch. When they investigate, they discover the cub is having a nightmare and the dog is comforting him. The player can talk to them and confirm that there's no danger. Subsequently, the cub will be a permanent feature in the camp, with new behaviours with Scratch, plus a new default dialogue.Note: if the player decides to not investigate the sounds, the animals will be moved off-stage for the remainder of the night/the sounds will stop, The player won't know what happened until they see the animals again. If they have SwA, they can learn that there was nothing wrong.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_OwlbearCub_CFM_Dog.json: The player is in camp at night when they hear an uproar and assume the owlbear cub has turned on Scratch, the camp dog. If the player investigates, they find the cub asleep and having a nightmare while Scratch lies beside him, howling softly to comfort him — there is no threat. If the player ignores the noise, the animals are moved off‑stage for the rest of the night (the sounds stop) and the player won’t know what happened until they see them again; players with Speak with Animals (SwA) can later learn there was nothing wrong. After this scene the cub becomes a permanent camp companion with new behaviours alongside Scratch and added default dialogue.
- CAMP_OwlbearCub.json: Default dialogue with the owlbear cub in the player's camp - available after the events of CAMP_OwlbearCub_CFM_Dog. The player can pet the cub, ask some SwA questions and learn what happened during the previous CFM if they opted to quit the dialogue early (what sounded like the owlbear cub attacking the dog was actually the cub having a bad dream and the dog comforting him).
- CAMP_OwlbearCub_CRD_2.json: IMPROTANT: If players help the cub in this dialog, it becomes the permamement camp follower.In SwA, the owlbear cub speaks in short staccato 'sentences.' He's vicious and feral - but scared. He's slightly injured, and playing it up more than it is, and he's distrustful of the player at first. If the player helps him, he becomes excited and runs off to hunt. In the next night, he returns with a dead bird.The owlbear has appeared in camp for a second night.  The player has previously spared the cub after killing its mother, and saved it from a cruel game run by the goblins in their camp.
He reacts much more suspiciously of the player if they antagonised him in their first encounter.
- CAMP_OwlbearCub_CRD_1.json: In SwA, the owlbear cub speaks in short staccato 'sentences.' He's vicious and feral - but scared. If the player coaxes him with food or is nice to him, he will cautiously consider approaching - but is scared off before he gets too close.An owlbear cub - young, but still dangerous - appears in camp. The player has previously spared the cub after killing its mother, and saved it from a cruel game run by the goblins in their camp.
The cub is scared, and quick to run or attack - it's an untamed wild animal.
- CAMP_Courier_Dog.json: In SwA, Scratch speaks like a human. He doesn't have any kind of dog-like affectation, nor is he stupid - he's well-spoken, even when he's saying 'dog' things.Scratch, the dog a dead courier we met during our travels, appears in our camp at night, having retrieved something. We can engage in a little tug of war in order to see what he's fetched.
